papers.title: The Work of Mathematical Production in the Age of AI
papers.abstract: The emergence of powerful artificial intelligence has unsettled the relationship between mathematical production and the human intellectual activity that mathematical artifacts have traditionally documented. We argue that mathematical practice cannot be adequately understood through the production of mathematical knowledge alone, and distinguish four interrelated dimensions of inquiry: knowledge, understanding, making sense, and figuring out. Building on Kitcher, Dewey, and subsequent philosophy of mathematical practice, we develop an expanded framework incorporating the cognitive and computational capacities of mathematical communities, their conceptual organizations, provisional investigative models, and the role of unsuccessful inquiry. We propose reconceptualizing artificial intelligence as a manifestation of physically organized computation whose mathematical behavior itself can become an object of experimental investigation. This perspective motivates a program of \emph{natural mathematics}, by which we mean the construction and comparison of artificial intellectual communities developing mathematical practices under different cognitive, conceptual, and normative conditions. Our aim is not simply to automate mathematical research or increase the production of theorems, but to investigate the robustness and contingency of mathematical concepts, the possibilities of alternative mathematical practices, and what such investigations might reveal about human mathematical cognition. Finally, we consider the future of human intellectual agency in a world where mathematical production need no longer depend upon humans. We argue for intergenerational epistemic stewardship as a justification for sustaining human mathematical traditions and opportunities for intellectual participation, independently of humanity's continued indispensability to mathematical progress.
